title: Dresden Codex (Maya manuscript)
summary: The Dresden Codex is a Maya screenfold book of 39 bark-bast sheets, probably made in the north or northeast of the Yucatán peninsula and likely copied from a classical-period model. It holds astronomical and calendar tables. The Dresden court librarian acquired it in Vienna in 1739; it was recognized as Maya in the 19th century.

uncertainty.note: SLUB: later post-classical period, ca. 1300-1521. mayan.org: radiocarbon dating of the bark paper suggests manufacture between 1210 and 1345 AD (citing Aimers and Rice). Range spans both.

where.modern_name: Yucatán Peninsula, Mexico (probable place of origin)

importance.justification: One of the few surviving pre-Hispanic Maya books, containing Venus and eclipse tables.
